name: National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan
watch: Aug-Sep 2026 show co-organised with sanctioned oligarch Vladimir Potanin's Olympic Collection.
records_note: The museum's site posts legal acts and anti-corruption pages but no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Funded by the Ministry of Culture. 2025 gifts of NT$5.64M came from property and building-materials firms, the E.SUN Foundation (bank), France's CCAC and individuals.
watch: State museum. Some donor names are masked in the filing. In Aug 2026 the Gwangju Biennale renamed its Taiwan Pavilion 'NTMoFA', a row not of the museum's making.
records_note: Annual reports 2017 to 2025, audited final accounts and dated donation lists are on its site; as a state agency it has no board.

name: NEON
funding: Private non-profit founded by collector Dimitris Daskalopoulos (food industry).
records_note: No annual report, accounts, funder list or board; the partners page names cultural partners, and the about page says only that NEON is a non-profit.

name: Netwerk Aalst
funding: Flemish Government Cultural Department, City of Aalst; independent non-profit arts institution.
watch: Independent center for contemporary art, artist cinema and research, with non-extractive labor practices.

name: Neuer Berliner Kunstverein (n.b.k.)
funding: Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion of Berlin, Stiftung Deutsche Klassenlotterie; non-profit art association.
watch: Houses one of Europe's oldest public video art collections (Video-Forum) and an Artothek lending library for citizens.

name: New Art Exchange
funding: £1.6M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £1.27M, about 79% of income; Power to Change (Freelands programme), Nottingham City Council, Nottingham Trent University, Art Fund.
watch: No flagged funder, protest or censorship found. Arts Council England is its main funder.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, funders show as one undated logo, and the board is listed.

name: New Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Trustee donations, gala, foundation grants, admission tickets, SANAA expansion capital campaign.

name: Newlyn Art Gallery
funding: Arts Council England and Cornwall Council together give 50 percent. Its support page also shows Bloomberg Philanthropies, Headley Trust, Linbury Trust, Wolfson Foundation, Ashden and DASH.
watch: 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies in May 2026. No campaign targets Newlyn.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, funders show as undated logos with no readable names, and trustees are listed.

name: Nezu Museum
funding: Chairman Koichi Nezu is honorary chairman of Tobu Department Store; councillor Yoshizumi Nezu chairs Tobu Railway.
watch: The claim that it takes no Tobu Group donations is not on its site. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Nezu posts yearly reports from FY2012, settled accounts and a full list of directors and councillors, and names no donors or sponsors.

name: Nguyen Art Foundation
funding: Founded 2018, privately funded by Quynh Nguyen, founder of flavour and fragrance firm Viet Huong JSC and co-founder of the EMASI schools. It works from its own financial resources.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, donor list or board found; the team page names the founder, director, manager and curator only.

name: Nhaka Gallery (formerly Gallery Delta)
funding: Operates under the Women's Gallery Arts and Research Trust. Its March 2023 show had support from the Swiss and Australian embassies and UN Women. No funder list is published.
watch: Gallery Delta was founded in 1975 by Derek Huggins and Helen Lieros, who died in 2021; Nhaka presents itself as continuing that legacy.
records_note: No Nhaka Gallery website was found; the only named backers are for one 2023 show, and no reports, accounts or board appear.

name: Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC)
funding: Funded directly by Reliance Industries (India largest fossil fuel petrochemical, refining, and telecom conglomerate) under billionaire Mukesh Ambani.
watch: Prestige vehicle of a billionaire's petro-industrial conglomerate; it stands for corporate dominance of public cultural space in Mumbai.
